guide.habit: Paste the error or name the files, and say what not to touch
guide.why: the real error text and the files involved tell the agent where to look; a limit stops it changing too much.
guide.try_this: paste the exact error or failing test, name the files it touches, and say what must not change.
guide.starter: Goal: <what done looks like>. Error or test: <paste it>. Files: <where to look>. Don't change: <what to leave alone>.
guide.counts: Counts when your request gives the goal, the context (such as a pasted error or file names) and a limit.

guide.habit: Name the reader, and give an example doc to copy
guide.why: a named reader and an example of the shape you want need far less rewriting than a description.
guide.try_this: say who will read it and what they should do after, and point at a past doc whose shape you like.
guide.starter: Write <doc> for <reader> so they can <decide or do what>. Follow the shape of <example doc>. Use <sources>. Keep it under <length>.
guide.counts: Counts when your request names the reader, the purpose and the limits, such as length or an example to follow.

guide.habit: Say what you'll do with the answer, and what you already know
guide.why: the reason behind a question and what you already know let the agent answer the right question.
guide.try_this: say what you'll do with the answer, what you already know, and where not to look.
guide.starter: I'm asking because <decision or task>. I already know <what you know>. Look at <where>, not <where not>. Answer: <question>.
guide.counts: Counts when your question says why you ask, what you already know, and where to look or not look.

guide.habit: Quote what was wrong, then add one new fact
guide.why: rewording alone rarely changes the result; the agent needs something new to go on.
guide.try_this: quote the line that was wrong, say why, and add one example, file or limit.
guide.starter: This part is wrong: "<quote>". Because <why>. Use <example, file or limit> and try again.
guide.counts: Counts when each follow-up adds something new, not only a rewording.

guide.habit: Ask for the test output in the reply
guide.why: seeing which tests passed is the quickest check that the change works.
guide.try_this: end your request with: run the tests and show me what passed and failed. Read it before you use the change.
guide.starter: <The change>. Then run <test command> and show me the diff and what passed and failed.
guide.counts: Counts when the result was checked before you used it, such as test output or a diff you read.

guide.habit: Ask for sources and open questions, then check them
guide.why: drafted claims can sound right and be wrong; the gaps the agent names are where to look first.
guide.try_this: ask for each claim's source and a list of what it was unsure of, then answer or fix each one.
guide.starter: List every factual claim in the draft with its source, then list what you were unsure of and why.
guide.counts: Counts when you checked the draft before using it, such as answering its open questions or checking sources.

guide.habit: Hand over the whole task with a "Done when" list
guide.why: with the whole task and a short done list, the agent can plan the steps and finish without asking you.
guide.try_this: describe the whole change, then add Done when with two or three things you can check, such as a test that passes.
guide.starter: <The whole change>. Done when: <test that passes>, <what you can see>, <what stays untouched>. Make all the edits, then show me the diff.
guide.counts: Counts when your request hands over the whole outcome and says what finished looks like.

guide.habit: Ask for the whole draft with a "Done when" list
guide.why: asking for the whole draft with what done means lets the agent keep it consistent.
guide.try_this: ask for the complete draft, and list the sections or questions a finished one must cover.
guide.starter: Write the whole <doc>. Done when it covers <sections> for <reader>. Then list what you were unsure of.
guide.counts: Counts when you ask for the whole draft and say what a finished one must cover.

guide.habit: Point the agent at the file and your notes
guide.why: when the agent reads your notes and writes the file, you review one draft instead of moving text back and forth.
guide.try_this: give the file path to write in and the notes or folder to read, then review the changes.
guide.starter: Write <doc> in <file path>. Read <notes or folder> first. When you're done, tell me what you changed and what you were unsure of.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent edits the file itself.

guide.habit: Give all your notes at once, then review the draft
guide.why: all your notes in one go let the agent shape the whole draft, and you review it once.
guide.try_this: collect your changes into one message, then review the next draft as a whole.
guide.starter: Revise <doc> with all of these: <change>, <change>, <change>. Then show me the full draft and list what you changed.
guide.counts: Counts when you don't steer the draft one small change per message.

guide.habit: Use agent mode and let it make the edits
guide.why: in agent mode the agent edits the files and runs commands itself, so you review one result instead of steering each step.
guide.try_this: in Copilot Chat pick Agent in the mode list; agree a short plan, say go, then review the diff once.
guide.starter: Plan <the change> in a few steps and wait for my go. Then make all the edits yourself and show me the diff.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent edits the files itself and you don't steer each small step.

guide.habit: Ask for the file, line or link behind each claim in the answer
guide.why: an answer can sound sure and still be wrong; a source you can open turns a guess into a fact.
guide.try_this: ask where each claim in the answer comes from, and open one source before you act on it.
guide.starter: Answer <question>. For each claim, give the file and line, or the link, it comes from, and say how sure you are.
guide.counts: Counts when you checked the answer before acting on it, such as opening a source or trying it.

guide.habit: Ask the whole question and say what a good answer covers
guide.why: the whole question and what a good answer covers lets the agent dig in and report back once.
guide.try_this: say what you need to decide and what a good answer must cover, then let the agent find it.
guide.starter: I need to decide <decision>. Find out <question>. A good answer covers <points>, with sources.
guide.counts: Counts when you ask the whole question and say what a good answer must cover.

guide.habit: Say "read the code and logs, don't guess"
guide.why: an agent that reads the files, logs or docs itself often finds what a pasted excerpt leaves out.
guide.try_this: name where to look and ask the agent to read it itself instead of pasting the material in.
guide.starter: Read <files, logs or docs> to answer <question>. Don't guess. Tell me what you read and what you found.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent reads, searches or runs something itself.

guide.habit: Put your follow-ups in the first ask
guide.why: one full ask lets the agent plan its search instead of waiting for your next nudge.
guide.try_this: put the follow-ups you expect into the first ask, then read the whole answer.
guide.starter: Find out <question>. Also cover <follow-up> and <follow-up>. Report back once, with sources.
guide.counts: Counts when you don't steer the agent one follow-up per message.

guide.habit: Say what should run, where, and what must not break
guide.why: an agent that knows what should run, where, and what must not break avoids most failed runs.
guide.try_this: say what should be running or released, in which place, and what must stay untouched.
guide.starter: Goal: <what should be running or released>. Where: <app, environment, account>. Must not: <what must not break or change>. Then: <the task>.
guide.counts: Counts when your request says what should run, where, and what must not change.

guide.habit: Name the proof: a version, a page loading or a log line
guide.why: a command can succeed while the app, release or tool still does not work.
guide.try_this: say what proves it worked, and ask the agent to show it before you move on.
guide.starter: After <the step>, show me proof it worked: <the version number, the URL loading, or the log line>.
guide.counts: Counts when you checked it worked before moving on.

guide.habit: Hand over the whole run with a done check and a stop
guide.why: an agent with the whole run, a done check and a stop point can do the steps and still leave you the risky one.
guide.try_this: give the whole outcome, how you'll know it's done, and the risky step (deploy, delete, push) where it must stop and ask.
guide.starter: Do <the whole release or run>. Done means <the check that passes>. Stop and ask before <the risky step>.
guide.counts: Counts when you hand over the whole run and say what done looks like.

guide.habit: Let the agent run the commands and fix errors
guide.why: an agent that runs the commands sees the errors itself and can fix them before it hands back.
guide.try_this: let the agent run each command, fix what fails, and report what each printed.
guide.starter: Run the commands yourself to <goal>. Fix errors as you go. Tell me each command and what it printed.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent runs the commands itself.

guide.habit: Give the whole run up front, not one command at a time
guide.why: with the whole run up front, the agent can do the steps and fix errors before it hands back.
guide.try_this: say the end state and the steps you expect, then let it run and report.
guide.starter: Get <app or release> to <end state>. Steps I expect: <step>, <step>. Stop and ask before <risky step>. Report each command and what it printed.
guide.counts: Counts when you don't steer the run one command per message.

guide.habit: Keep an instructions file in the repo and point to it
guide.why: an instructions file gives every task the same build, test and done rules, so the agent can plan alone.
guide.try_this: add .github/copilot-instructions.md or AGENTS.md with how to build, how to test and what done means, and name it in your request.
guide.starter: Read <instructions file>. Plan the steps, do them, and check each one against it.
guide.counts: Counts when you give the agent a written brief, spec or instructions file. Naming it in your request makes it clear.

guide.habit: Put the test command in your instructions file
guide.why: then every task ends with the agent running the tests and fixing what fails, without you asking.
guide.try_this: add a line such as: before you finish, run <test command> and fix what fails until it passes.
guide.starter: <The task>. Run the tests with <command>. Keep fixing until they all pass, then show me the diff and the test output.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent runs a test, build or lint command itself.

guide.habit: Ask the agent to run a link and spelling check
guide.why: an agent that runs the link and style checks can fix what fails before it hands back.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to run the doc checks, such as links and spelling, and fix what fails.
guide.starter: <The doc task>. Then run <doc check, such as markdownlint or a link check> and fix what fails. Show me the output.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent runs a doc check itself, such as markdownlint or a link check.

guide.habit: Have the agent run a smoke test after each step
guide.why: an agent that runs the smoke test or health check can fix what fails before it hands back.
guide.try_this: name the script that proves it works, such as a smoke or verify script, and ask the agent to run it after each step.
guide.starter: <The run or release>. After each step, run <smoke test or health check>. Fix what fails, then show me the output.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent runs a check itself, such as tests or a script named smoke, verify or check.

guide.habit: Give each step to a sub-agent, with a test between steps
guide.why: an automated check between steps catches a bad step before the next one builds on it.
guide.try_this: ask for a short plan, a sub-agent per step, and a test or check the agent runs before the next step starts.
guide.starter: Split <the task> into steps. Give each step to a sub-agent, and run <check> after each before going on.
guide.counts: Counts when sub-agents did the work and the agent ran a check.

guide.habit: Send one sub-agent per source, then merge
guide.why: each sub-agent reads one source well, and you get one combined answer back.
guide.try_this: name the sources and ask for one sub-agent each, then one answer with sources.
guide.starter: Split <question> by source: <source>, <source>, <source>. Send a sub-agent to each, then combine what they found into one answer with sources.
guide.counts: Counts when sub-agents looked into the parts of the question.

guide.habit: Prove each finding with a query or test
guide.why: an answer the agent has proved with a command, query or test can be reused without checking again.
guide.try_this: ask the agent to prove each finding with a command, query or test it runs.
guide.starter: Answer <question>. For each finding, run <command, query or test> that proves it, and show the output.
guide.counts: Counts when the agent runs a test or check command itself.

guide.habit: Save it as a prompt file and run it by name
guide.why: a saved prompt runs the same way every time, for you and for anyone you share it with.
guide.try_this: save the steps as a prompt file in .github/prompts, commit it, then start the next one by its name.
guide.starter: Turn what we just did into .github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md: its inputs, steps, checks, and when to stop and ask.
guide.counts: Not counted yet: AIQ can't tell when a saved workflow runs. It's still worth doing.
